title: GPT‑6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
titleZh: 适合所有人的 GPT‑6 和智能 UI
author: joshuawright11
relevanceReason: 命中 5 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Last month we introduced the first GPT‑6 models for paid customers and today we're bringing that next generation of intelligence to more people with a new GPT‑6 model built for more than 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week.GPT‑6 in ChatGPT introduces Intelligent UI, a new capability that allows ChatGPT to answer quickly with fully interactive user interfaces that make everyday answers more visual, make learning complex topics easier and that can quickly create a tool to solve a task right in the moment.Introducing Intelligent UIWe’ve trained GPT‑6 to compose responses using text, visuals and interactive elements, choosing how they fit together based on your question. With Intelligent UI, responses can include graphics, tappable buttons, forms, charts, and interactive experiences you can use directly in your conversation.The format depends on what you’re asking. A comparison might work best side by side. An explanation might be easier to understand through an interactive diagram. And when a simple text answer is the most useful response, ChatGPT can give you that.More visual responses to everyday questionsChatGPT can make a plan easier to follow by showing how it fits together. The timing for a Sunday roast can sit alongside the recipe, or the stops on a road trip can appear on a map, with notes on what’s worth a detour.Learn complex topics more easilyVisual and interactive explanations let you explore how something works, change an input to see what happens, or work through a problem step by step.Create interactive experiences just by askingYou can also ask ChatGPT to create a tool for the task at hand, such as a calculator to explore how savings could grow, a bill splitter for dinner with friends, or a game you can play in the conversation.How Intelligent UI worksWith Intelligent UI, we gave GPT‑6 the freedom to create the most useful interface for each question, while keeping the experience fast and familiar across web and mobile.We built a library of native, streamable components, along with a compiler that processes the interface as the model generates it. The library gives each response a familiar design foundation while leaving the model room to decide how the pieces fit together. The compiler allows the interface to appear progressively as the model generates it, without waiting for the entire response to be complete.We expanded our training methods to help the model make thoughtful decisions about content, layout, visuals, and interaction. This included evaluating the interfaces it creates for clarity, usefulness, and completeness. GPT‑6 learned to use the component library and make good design decisions, including how to organize information clearly, when to use interactivity, and when a simple text response is enough.There's still work ahead to improve the model's design judgment and expand what it can create, but Intelligent UI marks a significant shift in how people interact with ChatGPT. Instead of fitting every question into the same conversational format, ChatGPT can combine UI, data, and actions to create entirely new ways for people to explore, understand, and interact with information.Frontier Intelligence – delivered more quicklyWith GPT‑6, we’re also making it possible for ChatGPT to begin answering while it continues to think.GPT‑5.6 InstantGPT‑6 InstantWith the introduction of reasoning models, users could get help with much harder problems, but had to wait for the model to finish thinking before getting an answer. Now, ChatGPT can interleave thinking with answering. We trained it to take into account the user’s waiting time and progressively compose an answer using its knowledge and findings up to that point. It learned to build answers across multiple partial responses, each adding useful information without unnecessary filler, while keeping the full answer as cohesive and factual as one written all at once.In an internal evaluation of high-value, everyday agentic tasks, GPT‑6 Extra High is able to begin answering in the same amount of time as GPT‑5.6 Medium while achieving a better overall score than GPT‑5.6 Extra High.For questions that need web search, GPT‑6 Instant starts answering 44% sooner, on average, than GPT‑5.6 Instant.GPT‑6 also improves the quality of answers that require web search. It makes better decisions about when to look something up and more reliably finds information that supports its answer. In an internal evaluation of difficult problems, GPT‑6 correctly addressed the key aspect of the user’s question more often than GPT‑5.6.Deploying GPT‑6 safelyAs we bring more intelligent AI to more people, we work to improve how it recognizes real-world risks, how honestly it responds, and how well it respects the limits that people set. GPT‑6 makes progress in each of these areas, building on several of Astra’s safety advances to better resist attempts to bypass its safety training, follow safeguards, and be clearer about what it can and can’t do relative to GPT‑5.6 Sol. We updated its safety training based on lessons from real-world use to strengthen protections against high-risk misuse involving cyberattacks, biological threats, and violence. In adversarial testing, GPT‑6 showed stronger resistance to attempts to bypass its safety training, particularly attacks that adapt across multiple turns. GPT‑6 is also trained to respond safely in higher-risk scenarios while avoiding unnecessary refusals of harmless requests. This includes using conversation history and relevant context to recognize risks that may not be apparent from a single prompt.We ran alignment evaluations throughout training, assessing honesty and responses to safety restrictions. GPT‑6 is better at recognizing and communicating the limits of its own capabilities, including when it lacks the information or tools needed to answer. More detail on the results and our review is available in the system card⁠(opens in a new window).AvailabilityGPT‑6 with Intelligent UI starts rolling out globally to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise tiers today in the Chat tab. Starting tomorrow, the rollout expands to Free and Go tiers. Enterprise availability depends on workplace admin settings.GPT‑6 in ChatGPT is powered by GPT‑6 Sol for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers, and GPT‑6 Luna for Free and Go tiers. Both are tuned for everyday conversation.This update applies to the Chat experience in ChatGPT. The models powering Work and Codex are not changing as part of this release.What comes nextOur mission is to deliver the benefits of artificial general intelligence safely to all of humanity. GPT‑6 brings our latest advances in intelligence to the more than 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT every week.Intelligent UI is a step toward a ChatGPT that can shape an interface around what you’re trying to do.Over time, we want ChatGPT to create more of the interfaces people need for everyday tasks. You should be able to describe what you want to accomplish and work with an experience built around it.For decades, people have had to learn how to use software, navigating fixed interfaces designed around particular tasks. We believe the future will be different. Instead of people adapting to software, software will adapt to people.

comments.author: revolvingthrow
comments.textRawHtml:
I find the Sunday roast comparison of 5.6 vs 6 very interesting. I have no doubt most people will prefer 6, yet I am almost repulsed by all the images, so much needless whitespace, checklist and so on. Feels like I'm being condescended to and treated like a child.

Given that OpenAI is making noises about merging work with chat (a horrible idea imo), and Work is very similar to Codex... I dearly hope things like these won't have any meaningful cross-polination into the actual work tools.

Seeing that the chat is based on 6.0 and not 6.1 is disappointing. The "Visual and interactive explanations" seems genuinely useful, but 6.1 is just so much better. I wouldn't truly trust the 6.1 with the explanations, but I'd trust them a fair bit more than 6.0. I understand that compute isn't infinite, but tons of people only interact with the chat and having your "things-explainer" be as good as it can be is important when people increasingly treat AI models as the source of truth, or even use them for academic learning and whatnot.

Still, the models will improve, so the visual explainer seems pretty good as an idea / mvp.
comments.textZhHtml:
我发现 5.6 与 6 的周日烘焙比较非常有趣。我毫不怀疑大多数人会更喜欢 6，但我几乎对所有图像感到厌恶，那么多不必要的空白、清单等等。感觉我像个孩子一样受到屈尊和对待。

考虑到 OpenAI 正在发出关于将工作与聊天合并的声音（在我看来，这是一个可怕的想法），而且 Work 与 Codex 非常相似......我非常希望这样的事情不会与实际的工作工具产生任何有意义的异花授粉。

看到聊天是基于 6.0 而不是 6.1 是令人失望的。 “视觉和交互式解释”似乎确实有用，但 6.1 确实要好得多。我不会真正相信 6.1 的解释，但我比 6.0 更相信他们。我知道计算不是无限的，但很多人只与聊天互动，当人们越来越多地将人工智能模型视为真理的来源，甚至将它们用于学术学习之类的时候，让你的“事物解释器”尽可能好就很重要。

模型仍然会改进，所以视觉解释器作为一个想法/mvp似乎相当不错。

children.author: DriverDaily
children.textRawHtml:
> Feels like I'm being condescended to and treated like a child.

My most used prompt in the last week is probably "Explain this concisely and simply, like I am a child".

I spent years dumbing things down and creating visuals to support it for decision makers. I am frequently asking ChatGPT to do the same for me.
children.textZhHtml:
> 感觉自己像个孩子一样受到屈尊和对待。

上周我最常用的提示可能是“简洁明了地解释一下，就像我是个孩子一样”。

我花了数年时间简化事情并创建视觉效果来为决策者提供支持。我经常要求 ChatGPT 为我做同样的事情。

children.author: Terr_
children.textRawHtml:
Possibly also useful:

> ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English (STE) is a controlled natural language that is designed to simplify and clarify technical documentation. It was originally developed in the 1980s by the European Association of Aerospace Industries (AECMA) at the request of the European airline industry, which wanted a standardized form of English for aircraft maintenance documentation that could be easily understood by non-native English-speakers.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Technical_English
children.textZhHtml:
可能也有用：

> ASD-STE100 简化技术英语 (STE) 是一种受控自然语言，旨在简化和澄清技术文档。它最初是由欧洲航空航天工业协会 (AECMA) 应欧洲航空业的要求于 20 世纪 80 年代开发的，该协会希望为飞机维护文档提供一种标准化的英语形式，以便非英语母语人士能够轻松理解。

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Technical_English

children.author: PokeyCat
children.textRawHtml:
STE is very hyped for AI but has its own smells. It's designed for aircraft maintenance manuals, not software - the two don't share the same vocabulary used to "simply" describe something. I've had a coworker try and "simplify" our documentation with Claude applying STE and the results were equally appalling to read as the Claude-ism laden docs that came before, despite the reading level metrics going down on paper.

I've taken a liking to pointing agents at the Simple English Wikipedia editorial guidelines...but so much of that is for making up for shortcomings of modern Anthropic models. Codex running 6.1-sol explains things so much more clearly that I don't feel I need to assert a style guide on its output.
children.textZhHtml:
STE 对人工智能大肆宣传，但也有自己的味道。 它是为飞机维护手册而不是软件而设计的 - 两者不共享用于“简单”描述某事物的相同词汇。 我曾有一位同事尝试用 Claude 应用 STE 来“简化”我们的文档，结果读起来与之前充满 Claude 主义的文档一样令人震惊，尽管阅读水平指标已经写在纸上。

我喜欢在简单英语维基百科编辑指南中指向代理……但其中很大一部分是为了弥补现代人择模型的缺点。 运行 6.1-sol 的 Codex 解释得更加清楚，我觉得不需要在其输出上断言样式指南。

children.author: spockz
children.textRawHtml:
Gemini 3.8 for me always outputs in a concise way at the level understandable for any computer science masters graduate. Clear, to the point, a bit of formula for background when really required instead of the same formula in Prose, etc.

GPT stays too much in text imho.
children.textZhHtml:
Gemini 3.8 对我来说总是以任何计算机科学硕士毕业生都能理解的简洁方式输出。明确，切中要点，在真正需要时提供一些背景公式，而不是散文等中的相同公式。

GPT 在文本中保留太多，恕我直言。

children.author: criley2
children.textRawHtml:
In my experience

- Gemini 3.8 has a beautiful answer. Typography, use of lists, brevity, style, even the font choice on the web harness -- all of it is A tier or even S tier. Notice I didn't say answer quality. The answer is always extremely mid, and the harder the question (or more effort needed to answer it), Google just quits. I give it a "C" on answer quality

- ChatGPT (Chat, pre 6, I assume 5.6 although they commonly hide the model picker): Ugly answer. Runs on printing page after page of unnecessary side notes. Mostly just walls of texts in paragraphs with little thought to information design. However, inside of that mess of text is almost always the answer I'm looking for, and it's almost always incredibly better than the truncated, desgined Gemini answer.

For a while I ran all of my question queries on Gemini and ChatGPT, but I noticed that I basically always picked ChatGPT's answer head to head.
children.textZhHtml:
根据我的经验

- Gemini 3.8 给出了一个漂亮的答案。版式、列表的使用、简洁性、风格，甚至网络线束上的字体选择——所有这些都是 A 层甚至 S 层。请注意，我没有说答案质量。答案总是非常中间，问题越难（或者需要更多的努力来回答它），谷歌就会退出。我在答案质量上给它一个“C”

-ChatGPT（Chat，pre 6，我假设 5.6，尽管它们通常隐藏模型选择器）：丑陋的答案。逐页打印不必要的旁注。大部分只是段落中的文字墙，很少考虑信息设计。然而，在那堆混乱的文本中几乎总是我正在寻找的答案，而且它几乎总是比截断的、设计的 Gemini 答案好得多。

有一段时间，我在 Gemini 和 ChatGPT 上运行了所有问题查询，但我注意到我基本上总是直接选择 ChatGPT 的答案。

children.author: spockz
children.textRawHtml:
Interesting that this hasn’t been my experience. ChatGPT has often gave me with pages of text dripping with confidence about a solution for my problem. Diving very quickly into implementation details. Even if I tell it to stay in the problem and product fit level. Gemini on the other hand somehow always outputs at the level that I am expecting and reasoning.

I even found it was capable of stepping back from code implementation and bug hunting to “hang on, it’s not the algorithm that is incorrectly implemented, it is the wrong algorithm for the goal.” GPT Sol (5.6,6 and 6.1) just kept hammering in the problem.
children.textZhHtml:
有趣的是，这并不是我的经历。 ChatGPT 经常给我提供几页文字，充满信心地告诉我问题的解决方案。快速深入了解实施细节。即使我告诉它留在问题和产品适合的水平。 另一方面，Gemini 总是以我期望和推理的水平输出。

我什至发现它能够从代码实现和 bug 寻找中退一步，“坚持下去，这不是算法实现不正确，而是算法实现了错误的目标。” GPT Sol（5.6、6 和 6.1）一直在解决这个问题。

children.author: criley2
children.textRawHtml:
To be clear, I'm discussing non-technical use of Gemini and ChatGPT through the web harness.

While I do rarely use the web harnesses for technical research, nearly all of my technical questions are going through coding harnesses and layers of my local context, skills, etc, so what I produce from codex/claude code is not comparable to what others produce.

So my comparison of the web harnesses is me asking questions about caring for my baby, or product comparisons of new televisions, or visualizing a room organized differently (google sucked at this so bad, chatgpt did great), or asking for help in a video game, or other normie AI uses lol

I will say, Gemini is the best for asking about google services, such as Flights or Youtube.

Yup.

My go to phrase that I’ve found to work well is “please restate in high school English with direct declarative sentences and no parentheticals or references that require recalling previous turns of this conversation”

Which I have as a hotkey.
